chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Saeed al-A'raj, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a cooking pot in which there is a camel, and an amount of one 'Uqiyyah of blood had fallen into it; is it permissible to eat? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, because the fire consumes the blood.'

key_terms.أُوقِيَّةٍ: A unit of liquid measurement (approx. 12-13 oz)

ai.seo_question: Is food permissible to eat if blood falls into the cooking pot?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that a small quantity of blood (one Uqiyyah) falling into a cooking pot does not render the meat impure, as the cooking process (fire) effectively consumes or purifies it. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that heat acts as a purifying agent for minor contaminants in food, distinguishing it from cases requiring explicit removal or washing.
